🌱 Basics · Lesson 6 · 2 min read

AI Ethics & Safety

Bias, deepfakes and privacy — and how to use AI responsibly.

When AI is unfair

AI learns from data created by people, so it can also learn people's unfairness. This is called bias. In 2018, news reports revealed that Amazon had dropped an experimental hiring tool because it was biased against women: it had learned from ten years of CVs that mostly came from men. Researchers have also found that some face-recognition systems make far more mistakes with darker-skinned women than with lighter-skinned men. Fixing bias needs diverse data, careful testing and people checking the results.

Deepfakes and misinformation

Generative AI can create realistic fake photos, videos and voices, called deepfakes. They can be fun in films and memes, but they're also used to spread lies and to scam people — for example, by faking a relative's voice on the phone to ask for money. Before you share something shocking, stop and check: Who posted it? Do trusted news sources report it? Fakes keep getting better, so checking the source matters more than looking for glitches.

Did you know? Scammers can copy a voice from just a few seconds of audio. Agree on a secret family code word to use in emergencies.

Protect your privacy

AI systems learn from huge amounts of data, including things people post online. What you type into an AI tool may be stored and even used to train future models. Never share passwords, your home address, private photos or secrets with a chatbot, and check the privacy settings of the apps you use.

Humans stay in charge

When AI makes a mistake, the people who build and use it are responsible. That's why important decisions — in medicine, in courts or in hiring — should always be checked by a human. Governments are making rules too: the European Union's AI Act, adopted in 2024, is one of the world's first big laws on AI. And you have a role: use AI honestly, say when it helped you with schoolwork, and keep thinking for yourself.

Key points

  • AI can copy unfairness (bias) from the data it learns from.
  • Deepfakes are getting realistic: check the source before you share.
  • Protect your privacy, and keep humans responsible for important decisions.

Check yourself

Why can an AI system be unfair (biased)?

  1. It learned from data that contained human unfairness or was one-sided
  2. Computers have their own opinions about people
  3. AI is always programmed to be unfair on purpose
Show the answer

AI copies patterns from its training data — including unfair ones. Diverse data, testing and human checks help reduce bias.
